currentContext.business: Endurance Technologies Limited manufactures a diversified portfolio of automotive components encompassing aluminium die casting and machining, suspension systems, braking systems (including disc brakes and ABS), transmission components, alloy wheels and embedded electronics such as ABS ECUs and Battery Management Systems. It serves major Indian and global OEMs across the two-wheeler, three-wheeler and four-wheeler segments from strategically located plants in India and Europe, and is extending into electric-mobility components such as lithium-ion battery packs and into non-automotive applications including niche components for solar power generation plants. The business is supported by five DSIR-approved R&D centres and next-generation Suspension and Brakes R&D facilities focused on proprietary technologies.

Transmission: Adler technology-based Assist and Slip (APTC) clutch
Non-automotive: Niche components for solar power generation plants

currentContext.expansion: The Company continued to make progress on its greenfield and expansion projects during FY 2025-26. In October 2025 production commenced at the AURIC Bidkin plant in Dist. Chh. Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, for alloy wheels, with an installed capacity of 3.6 million wheels per annum. It is poised to commence production at its AURIC Shendra plant in Dist. Chh. Sambhajinagar for the manufacture of machined aluminium castings catering to four-wheelers and non-automotive applications. A lithium-ion battery pack plant is being set up at Mindewadi in Pune, Maharashtra, to cater to growing demand from EV and energy storage applications. In addition, the Company is establishing new capacities across various locations for braking systems, ABS and electronics, while also setting up a new aluminium forging facility to support increasing customer demand. On the inorganic side, wholly-owned subsidiary Endurance Overseas SpA acquired a 60% stake in Stöferle GmbH, Germany and Stöferle Automotive GmbH, Germany on 2nd April, 2025 — companies specialising in machining of aluminium castings for automotive applications and manufacture of CNC machines for captive use — strengthening the European footprint and capabilities in automation and advanced manufacturing. On 16th May 2025 the Company increased its shareholding in Maxwell Energy Systems Private Limited to 100%, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary and strengthening its presence in advanced electronics and battery management systems.

risks.note: The global economy remains susceptible to renewed trade disruptions and geopolitical escalations; escalating tensions in West Asia could disrupt key energy supply routes and trigger volatility in global oil markets, impacting fuel prices, logistics costs and industrial production.

risks.risk: Tightening emission and safety regulation and evolving EV policy
risks.note: The industry operates in a dynamic regulatory environment characterised by tightening emission and safety norms and evolving fuel efficiency and Electric Vehicle policies, which drive product re-engineering and compliance investment.

risks.risk: Supply chain constraints and rising compliance costs
risks.note: Explicitly flagged by the Board as a challenge for the industry alongside the regulatory environment, affecting input availability and cost.

risks.risk: Demand-side pressure from affordability and financing conditions
risks.note: The Board flags affordability and financing conditions as demand-side pressures; volume growth in FY 2025-26 was itself partly a function of the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation lowering cost of ownership, making demand sensitive to policy support.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition in the auto component landscape
risks.note: The competitive landscape is intensifying with global OEM participation, new EV entrants and increasing focus on technology, localisation and innovation.

A significant minority share of consolidated total income is generated by overseas operations, and European auto sales grew only modestly (about 1.8% year-on-year in FY 2025-26), so Europe remains a slower-growth, macro-exposed part of the portfolio.

risks.risk: Concentration on a major OEM customer
risks.note: New business wins from OEMs in India are reported excluding orders from one of the Company's major OEM customers, indicating a single customer relationship large enough to be disclosed separately.

Accelerating EV adoption, ADAS advancement and record BEV market shares in advanced markets are reshaping the components industry, requiring continuous reinvestment to keep the ICE-linked portfolio relevant.

one-line thesis: Endurance delivered strong Q4FY26 volume-led growth (Consol Rev +37.3% YoY) driven by 2W recovery and new EV wins, though margins faced pressure from commodity inflation and one-off Hero Electric provisions. The strategic pivot is accelerating with dual-channel ABS, in-house ECU production, and major greenfield SOPs (Battery packs, US EV OEM castings) set to drive FY27-FY29 optionality despite near-term energy cost headwinds.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Consol ₹4,116cr (+37.3% YoY), Standalone ₹2,975cr (+31.1% YoY). EBITDA: Consol ₹598cr (+30.8% YoY, 14.5% margin), Standalone ₹371cr (+13.7% YoY, 12.5% margin). PAT: Consol ₹276cr (+12.8% YoY), Standalone ₹210cr (+20.5% YoY). Order Book: Cumulative wins since FY22 (ex-Maxwell/Battery) ₹5,323cr peaking FY29; FY26 India wins ₹1,596cr. Net Debt: Not explicitly quantified in transcript, but Capex heavy (₹800cr FY26). One-offs: ₹6cr inventory provision (Hero Electric) impacted Maxwell EBITDA; ₹73.7cr non-value-add raw material (Alloy/Steel) inflation suppressed standalone margin by ~70bps (normalized ~13.3%); Q4FY25 had ₹25cr one-time gains not repeated.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Strong double-digit growth expected driven by new SOPs; 4W mix to rise from 6% towards 10%+ medium term. Margin: Q1FY27 volatile due to energy/commodity costs; normalization expected from Q2FY27 assuming pass-throughs. Order Inflow: Robust pipeline (Maxwell RFQs >₹300cr). Capex: FY27 budget similar to FY26 (~₹800cr), focused on automation and new plants.
order book & pipeline: Total cumulative orders (since FY22, ex-Maxwell/Battery) ₹5,323cr (₹4,593cr new) peaking FY29. FY26 India wins ₹1,596cr (₹1,579cr new). EV-specific wins ₹1,724cr p.a. (incl. Maxwell/Battery). Europe FY26 orders €15.8mn. Key ramp-ups: AURIC Shendra (peak ₹513cr), Battery Pack (₹300-600cr), Maxwell (₹247cr p.a. peak Q2FY27).
segment / subsidiary detail: Braking: ABS capacity expanding by 12L units (SOP Sep-26); Dual-channel ABS SOP Jun-26 (Bajaj); Chennai disc brake plant SOP Jul-26 (Royal Enfield). Suspension: Inverted forks ramping to 100k units/month by FY27 end. EV Electronics: Maxwell turnover ₹162cr (+131% YoY); Battery pack SOP started May-26. Casting: AURIC Shendra SOP Jun-26 (US EV OEM, JLR). Alloy Wheels: 4.8M units capacity; new customers (Honda, Suzuki). Solar: ₹345cr wins (dampers/actuators).
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Regulatory tailwind: ABS mandate expansion to lower cc vehicles (12L new capacity). 2) EV Penetration: In-house BMS/ECU integration increasing value-add; Battery pack SOP for 2W/3W. 3) 4W Diversification: Major wins from US EV OEM, JLR, Tata, Mahindra driving mix shift from 6% to 10%+ revenue. 4) Aftermarket: AI-enabled platform and mechanic loyalty program targeting long-term high-margin growth.
margins & cost dynamics: Standalone margin compressed to 12.5% (vs 13.3% normalized) due to ₹73.7cr alloy/steel inflation (non-value-add) and outsourcing costs (₹31.3cr) from volume surge. Energy costs up 50% (fuel) and 3x (gas vs 2021) in Europe; pass-through negotiations ongoing. Q1FY27 expected volatile; margin recovery targeted from Q2FY27. Maxwell margin impacted by ₹6cr Hero Electric provision.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex ₹800cr (India); FY27 guidance similar (~₹800cr). Focus on automation, new greenfield plants (Chennai brakes, Sambhajinagar forging, SMT line), and capacity expansion (ABS, forks).
capital allocation: Inorganic: Stöferle acquisition completed Apr-25 (performing above expectations). Organic: Heavy reinvestment in greenfield capacities (AURIC, Chennai, Battery plant). Incentives: Maharashtra PSI scheme enhanced to ₹858cr (GST refund over 7 years).
risks & watch-items: 1) Commodity & Energy Volatility: Persistent high gas/oil/alloy prices with lagged pass-throughs. 2) Geopolitical: Middle East conflict impacting shipping/logistics. 3) Regulatory Delay: Potential deferral or modification of ABS mandate. 4) Execution: Ramp-up risks across multiple simultaneous greenfield SOPs. 5) Europe Macro: High energy costs and Chinese OEM competition.
management quality / tone: Confident on volume growth and order book quality; cautious on near-term margins due to external cost shocks (war, commodities); assertive on customer negotiations for price hikes; strategic focus on 'China+1' beneficiaries and EV transition.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) Backward Integration: In-house ECU production for ABS (single-channel started, dual-channel Jun-26) to capture margin leakage. 2) Fuel Switch: Tier-2 suppliers switched from gas to furnace/diesel oil to mitigate availability/cost risks. 3) Aftermarket Tech: First in industry to deploy AI-enabled platform for secondary order maximization. 4) Solar Diversification: Significant non-auto revenue stream emerging (₹345cr wins) from US/Spanish clients.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation and energy costs suppressing near-term margins despite volume growth | Bajaj Auto Ltd | beneficiary | High | Primary beneficiary of dual-channel ABS SOP (Jun-26) and expanded capacity; strong volume growth passed through supply chain. |
| High energy costs in Europe and supply chain disruptions | Tata Motors Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Key winner in 4W casting and braking (SOP Jun-26); benefits from China+1 strategy and local sourcing mandates. |
| Intense competition in EV battery space and regulatory hurdles | Hero MotoCorp Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential beneficiary of ABS mandate and suspension upgrades, though transcript notes Hero Electric provision impact on Maxwell (unrelated to core Hero Moto). |

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
